title: fix(plugin-hono-server): end a graceful close with its last in-flight request; cut or budget seven slow Test Core cases
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"marchtian"} -->
_Requested by **田騏** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01VmuUhXU9SSUzqJYyXSmYSi?thread=cmsg_01VmuUhXU9SSUzqJYyXSmYSiNjyvCdXYygFqntMNR7S2dW)_

Fixes #30920

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：Hono 服务器优雅关闭时，正在处理的请求一结束就关掉它自己的连接（未发响应头的回 `Connection: close`，已发 keep-alive 头的在全部字节发完后只关自己这条连接，不碰别的连接）；关闭期间的连接记账按连接存放、连接断开即清掉；另外七条慢用例里两条砍掉重复工作、四条按「CI 最慢读数 ×3」给了单独超时，一条经测量不需要改。
- 为什么改：两条 drain 用例在空闲机器上也要 3–4 秒，实测原因是关闭时还在跑的请求结束后变成空闲 keep-alive 连接，服务器要等客户端自己断开（fetch 3 秒、node 代理 4 秒）；线上服务关闭同样会白等这段时间。其余七条在 CI 上已用到 5 秒默认超时的一半以上，负载一高就会把 main 和合并队列变红。
- 风险与回滚：生产代码只改 `plugin-hono-server` 的关闭路径；一条响应结束时只释放它自己的连接，别的连接上还在发送的大响应不受影响（有慢读者 32 MiB 用例钉住），流水线请求在连接断开后不再被留在内存里；drain 超时强关的兜底不变；其余都是测试文件。回滚就是 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/adapter.ts` 的 `trackForDrain`、`responsesOwedOn` 与 `close()`；`adapter-drain.test.ts` 新增的慢读者、流水线断连与迟到请求头三条用例；`packages/client/src/auth-rotated-session-token.test.ts` 模块顶层新增的 `fileServer()` 预建。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-hono-server exec vitest run src/adapter-drain.test.ts src/adapter-tls-listener.test.ts --reporter=verbose`，应看到 12 条全过，两条 drain 用例约 0.2 秒（改前 3.2 秒与 4.2 秒）。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

**The drain (`packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/adapter.ts`, patch changeset).** `close()` calls `closeIdleConnections()` once, when the drain starts. A connection whose request is still running at that moment is skipped, and Node never runs the release again. When the response ends, the connection becomes an idle keep-alive socket, and `server.close()` waits until the client drops it. The client drops it after the server's `Keep-Alive: timeout=5` hint minus its own margin: 3 s for `fetch` (undici) and 4 s for the `node:http(s)` agent. Measured with a socket trace (see Tests): the response finishes at about 220 ms, the server socket waits with a 6000 ms timer, and `close()` resolves only when the client sends FIN, at 3232 ms (`fetch`) and 4216 ms (agent).

During a drain the adapter now does two things:

- a response whose headers are not written yet goes out with `Connection: close`, so Node ends the socket once it is sent and the client knows not to reuse it. This covers responses in flight when `close()` starts, and requests whose headers finish arriving on an open connection after the drain began;
- a response whose keep-alive headers were already sent when the drain began (a stream, for example) ends its OWN connection with `destroySoon()` once it has finished (every byte handed to the socket) and no other response on that connection is pending. It never calls the server-wide `closeIdleConnections()`: Node counts a response as done once it has called `end()`, before its bytes are flushed, so a sweep at that moment would destroy any other connection whose response is ended but still flushing to a slow reader.

The drain bookkeeping is kept per connection (`responsesOwedOn`) and dropped when the connection closes. A response pipelined behind another never gets a socket if the connection dies, so it never emits `'close'`; keying by connection keeps it from being held until `close()`. The drain window still force-closes whatever outlasts it.

**The seven other cases.** Each budget follows the rule PR #30919 used: 3x the slowest `Test Core` reading on the card, rounded up to the next second, with the readings and the arithmetic in a comment at the case. No global timeout, no skip, no retry.

| Case | Action | Local before (ms) | Local after (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metadata-protocol` two derivations of the same schemas agree exactly | **cut**: one derivation compared with the module-load singleton, not two plus the singleton | 743 / 844 / 775 | 353 / 372 / 410 |
| `client` login → enable → verifyTotp → disable → deleteUser | **cut**: the file's shared server and its better-auth instance are built at module scope, out of the first case's clock | 729 / 800 / 743 | 566 / 583 / 558 |
| `driver-sql` sql-driver.ts and the modules split out of it contain none of them | budget 8000 (3 x 2499 = 7497; the reading is 1 ms under the rule's over-half-the-default line, and the comment says why it takes the budget anyway) | 469 / 442 | 433 / 313 / 432 |
| `plugin-security` posture single/group/isolated hidden-column cases | budget 9000 (3 x 2949 = 8847) | 624-694 | 489-669 |
| `plugin-sharing` a refused upgrade write does not block the read | budget 8000 (3 x 2605 = 7815) | 545 / 458 / 689 | 499 / 398 / 474 |
| `cli` the census reaches the live tree | budget 8000 (3 x 2629 = 7887) | 1291 / 1243 / 1102 | 1117 / 1234 / 1217 |
| `cli` the boot this sweep reads from really did compose the deployment | **no change**, see Acceptance notes | 10222 / 11341 / 10996 | n/a |

## Tests

`adapter-drain.test.ts` pins each part:

- the in-flight case asserts the response carried `Connection: close`;
- a streamed response whose keep-alive headers went out before `close()` completes, and `close()` resolves less than 1000 ms after its body ends (the defect waits about 3000 ms);
- a raw connection writes half a request's headers, `close()` starts, the rest arrives: the answer is `Connection: close`;
- a slow reader's 32 MiB response calls `end()` during the drain and is still flushing (asserted) when another keep-alive stream ends: every byte arrives;
- four pipelined requests on one raw connection, the connection destroyed: the drain bookkeeping holds none of them afterwards.

Ablation, one part at a time, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` on head `586338ffbd` (the tests import `./adapter` from source, so no build is involved; each restore verified as blob == HEAD with an empty `git diff HEAD`):

- the round-1 server-wide `closeIdleConnections()` in place of the own-socket release: the slow-reader case goes red, `expected 3919730 to be 33554432` bytes;
- without dropping a connection's entry on its `'close'`: the pipelined case goes red, `expected 3 to be +0`;
- without the request-time `Connection: close` line: the late-headers case goes red, `expected 'keep-alive' to be 'close'`.

The whole new test file against the round-1 `adapter.ts` (`2ff6bb0735`): the slow-reader case fails (`expected 3919730 to be 33554432`) and the pipelined case fails (the round-1 set holds responses, so its retained count reads `NaN` against the expected 4); the late-headers case passes, as the round-1 code had that line.

<details><summary>Socket trace of close() with one request in flight (before / after)</summary>

Before (`fetch`):

```
[   56 ms] close() called
[  219 ms] server: response finished; shouldKeepAlive=true _last=false
[  224 ms] client: status 200, connection=keep-alive, keep-alive=timeout=5
[  226 ms] server socket after finish: timeout=6000
[ 3232 ms] server socket: "end" (peer, the client, sent FIN)
[ 3232 ms] close() resolved
```

Before (`node:http` agent, keepAlive): FIN from the client and `close()` resolved at 4216 ms. With `agent: false` (no keep-alive) `close()` resolved at 215 ms, which isolates the keep-alive wait as the cause.

After (`fetch`):

```
[   59 ms] close() called
[  227 ms] server: response finished; shouldKeepAlive=false _last=true
[  228 ms] close() resolved
[  237 ms] client: status 200, connection=close
```

</details>

<details><summary>Drain cases, local, before / after</summary>

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `adapter-tls-listener.test.ts` drains on close exactly as the plain listener does | 4209 ms | 214 ms |
| `adapter-drain.test.ts` lets an in-flight request complete instead of aborting it | 3233 ms | 268 ms |

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- **`cli` unmanaged-tables "the boot this sweep reads from really did compose the deployment" is not changed.** Timing trace (instrumented locally, not committed): the case body takes 1-2 ms, its `afterEach` 3 ms, and its `beforeEach` 10038-10378 ms, nearly all of it the first `bootSchemaStack` of the worker. vitest reports hooks inside a case's duration, but the 5 s `testTimeout` clocks only the body; this `beforeEach` declares its own `180_000`. So the 5 s default cannot time this case out, and a per-case timeout on a 2 ms body would change nothing. The later cases in the file boot in 90-145 ms. The local readings are on a box shared with other builds; the card's CI reading is 3295 ms.
- **`client` keeps no budget, by the file's own rule.** Its header says a recurrence is answered by cutting the case's own work, ⛔ not by a timeout, and its pin ④ refuses a numeric per-case timeout. The cut above moves arrangement out of the clock; what is left is the probe itself (a sign-up and five password or TOTP checks).
- **Found, not fixed here:** a response that has called `end()` but is still flushing at the moment `close()` STARTS is destroyed mid-body. Node's own `server.close()` sweeps idle connections (Node 19+), and the adapter's call at drain start does the same; both treat an ended response as done before its bytes are flushed. Reproduced on this branch with the slow-reader case reordered so the big response ends before `close()`: `expected 3919702 to be 33554432` bytes. That path is unchanged from `main`; reported to the seat for a card.
- No other file changes. The drain fix is a published-package change, so it ships a `patch` changeset; the test-only changes in the other six packages publish nothing.

## Verification

Head `586338ffbd` (round 2, on the round-1 merge of `origin/main` at `8ef4d30905`; the delta against `main` is these nine files).

- Typecheck, each touched package: `plugin-hono-server`, `client`, `metadata-protocol`, `plugin-security`, `plugin-sharing`, `driver-sql`, `cli`: all exit 0.
- Tests: `plugin-hono-server` 481/481 on round 2 (478/478 on round 1), `client` 712/712, `metadata-protocol` 22525 passed / 26 skipped, `plugin-security` 5820 passed / 45 skipped, `plugin-sharing` 1445/1445, `driver-sql` 3867 passed / 218 skipped, `cli --project unit` 5603/5603. The `cli` integration layer is left to CI.
- Gates derived by `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` on `586338ffbd`: 69 families, 69 run, all exit 0; `--ran` reconciliation: 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN. `check:tenant-audit-census` first flagged the new set's `.delete()` receiver; the set is now a named type in the adapter, and the census passes. `check:dts-closure` and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` first read a `dist/` that was being rebuilt and went red on missing files; rerun on the finished build, both exit 0.
